first_impression.reaction: I googled this because James floated 'just do the legal bit at home and party in Italy' and I wanted to know what the paperwork actually is. First paragraph: what it is, who gets it, one month to 18 months, and no NOIM, no wedding. Second paragraph tells me it doesn't apply at all if we marry legally overseas. That's the exact fork we're at. No 'dream day' nonsense. Kept reading.

journey.quote: If you plan to marry legally in another country instead, the NOIM does not come into it: you follow that country's rules.
journey.reaction: Answered my real question in the second paragraph instead of making me scroll for it. Appreciated.

journey.quote: For a couple who books a venue two summers ahead, that means the date is often secured long before the paperwork can begin.
journey.reaction: That's us. We're about 14 months out, so we're already inside the window. Small detail, but it's the kind of thing someone who's actually run these timelines would point out.

journey.quote: Treat that as a floor, not a target.
journey.reaction: Good. The separate in-person meetings with the celebrant is something I wouldn't have known to diary. Practical, not preachy.

journey.section: How to fill out the NOIM form step by step
journey.quote: Each of you completes your own details on the form. If you are unsure about any field, the Attorney-General's Department's advice is to ask your authorised celebrant for help with the form.
journey.reaction: The 'step by step' is a bit thin. Step 2 is basically 'fill it in, ask your celebrant'. Not wrong, and I'd rather that than made-up advice, but I skimmed the rest of the steps.

journey.section: Lodging a NOIM when you live overseas
journey.quote: Your authorised witness must be outside Australia with you, cannot be a celebrant, and must witness in person, because a NOIM for a couple outside Australia cannot be witnessed online.
journey.reaction: By this point I've read the overseas witness rule in the takeaways, the witness section, here, and again in the FAQ. We live in Sydney. Meanwhile the bit that does apply to us, who can witness in Australia, just says 'listed on the form'.

journey.section: Can the one-month notice be shortened?
journey.quote: Approval is never automatic, so start with your celebrant and treat a shortening of time as a fallback, not a plan.
journey.reaction: Honest. Doesn't pretend there's a loophole. That's what I want from anyone touching the legal side.

journey.section: Option A: marry legally in Australia, celebrate abroad
journey.quote: The celebration abroad can then be whatever you want it to be.
journey.reaction: This is the route I'm sending James. Small legal ceremony in Sydney with the grandparents who can't fly, then the real party overseas without a registrar dictating the day. Now I can actually picture it.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but you may not be able to use it for a name change, so check with your local registry.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that, and it matters to me. That's an honest trade-off between the two routes, plainly stated.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Either way, the legal steps stay with you and your celebrant or the local authority. The celebration is where we come in.
journey.reaction: Clear about who does what. I prefer that to a planner who claims to 'handle everything' and then doesn't.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the celebration abroad, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing up front speak straight to my currency and hidden-cost worries. But if we go Option A, who lines up the Sydney legal date with the overseas celebration? 'Single point of contact' for the celebration only leaves that gap open.

unanswered_questions: If we marry legally in Sydney first, does our Wedded Advisor plan the overseas celebration around that date, or do we coordinate the two ourselves?
Can you suggest a celebrant for the small legal ceremony at home, or is that entirely on us?
Have you planned a wedding where the couple married legally at home and celebrated abroad, and can we see it (venue and date)?
If we go the legal-abroad route instead, does the Wedded Advisor help with the CNI and local paperwork, or only point us to the embassy?
Who, in practice, can witness the NOIM for a couple living in Sydney?
would_share_with: James: the intro and the two options (A and B), so we can decide where the legal bit happens
Mum and Dad (contributing): Option A, so they understand the 'real' wedding in Sydney can be small and the overseas one still counts as the celebration

cta_reaction.quote: When the legal route is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=notice-of-intended-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and telling me to settle the legal route first actually makes me trust them more. AUD quotes and the fee in writing tick boxes. But this is a paperwork explainer, and I'm nowhere near enquiring off one post. I'd want to see a real wedding that did the legal-at-home, celebrate-abroad split, and a destination guide or two, before I fill in a form.

top_3_changes: In 'Option A: marry legally in Australia, celebrate abroad', after 'The celebration abroad can then be whatever you want it to be.', say plainly whether the Wedded Advisor plans the overseas celebration around the Australian legal date or whether the couple coordinates the two. The line 'The celebration is where we come in.' leaves the hand-off between the Sydney ceremony and the trip unclear.

Cut the repeated overseas-witness rule (it appears in the key takeaways, 'Who can witness', 'Lodging a NOIM when you live overseas' and the FAQ) down to one full mention, and use the space in 'Witnessing in Australia' to tell Australia-based couples, if the source supports it, what kinds of people are on the authorised witness list rather than only 'listed on the form'.

Near 'The celebration abroad can then be whatever you want it to be.' or the closing 'Planning the celebration' section, link a real Wedded Wonderland wedding (venue and date) where the couple married legally at home and celebrated abroad. That is the proof that would move me from reading to enquiring.
